channel.title: The Valley Times-News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Valley Times-News (valleytimes-news.com)

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Loran Smith: Ginkgo Tree
item.description: From Athens sidewalks to Hiroshima's blast zone, the ancient ginkgo biloba proves its resilience, beauty, and quirks—from foul-smelling females to dazzling golden fall canopies.

item.title: Annual sheriff’s fundraiser supports local Girls Ranch
item.description: Chambers County Sheriff’s annual Grillin’ for Girls steak fundraiser returns March 7 in Valley, raising money for Tallapoosa County Girls Ranch.

item.title: Valley Parks and Rec proposes an indoor play area
item.description: Valley Parks and Rec may turn underused racquetball courts into a “Riverlands” indoor playground, offering play for kids on hot, cold and rainy days if city leaders approve.

item.title: Chambers Academy defeats Springwood for state championship
item.description: Chambers Academy edged rival Springwood 45-41 to claim the AISA 2A boys state title in a historic state championship meeting between the two teams.

item.title: Student-led health session coming to LaFayette
item.description: Auburn pre-health students will host a free preventive health session on Feb. 28 at LaFayette’s Chambers County Community Health and Wellness Center.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - John Tures: Oppose Those Who Portray Politicians Or Other People As Animals
item.description: John Tures traces ugly animal caricatures of politicians from Andrew Jackson to the Obamas and Trump, warning that dehumanizing art fuels division and undermines criticism.

item.title: Parks and Rec camp springs to life
item.description: Valley Parks and Rec launches spring break camp, a pilot for future youth programs, with daily activities and open registration through March 25.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - L. Michelle Moore: Picking Up Pecans
item.description: In a Georgia town strewn with uncollected pecans, L. Michelle Moore finds a lesson in gratitude—and a parallel to how we overlook abundant solar energy.

item.title: Valley tree giveaway returns next month
item.description: Valley residents can snag free fruit trees March 14 as the city’s annual Tree Giveaway returns, offering about 400 saplings first-come, first-served at City Hall.

item.title: Two Valley florists see busiest time of year
item.description: As Valentine’s Day drives a surge in orders, two longtime Valley florists juggle family help, rising tariffs and changing tastes in roses to get hundreds of arrangements delivered.
